VBO:0201452.summary: Local keepers describe Zerdavas as strongly attached to their owners, with an enduring place in hunting and guarding. In the eastern Black Sea mountains, traditional hunters use them as barking pointers, generally tracking quietly before giving voice when quarry is found. Wild boar is an important part of that regional working history.
VBO:0201452.shortDescription: A devoted regional hunting and guard dog, traditionally used as a barking pointer in the Black Sea mountains.

sources.title: Sözüer et al. — Zerdava field report, PADS Journal48 (2018)
sources.evidence: Methodspp7–8 and direct accountpp7/14 support owner attachment explicitly attributed to local keepers; huntingpp7/14/16–18 describes barking pointer, generally quiet tracking then voice at located game, especially regional wildboar. Morphologypp9–11 records compact medium-small body, erect triangular ears, deep ribs/developed neck/shoulders, relatively large paws, liver/white ticking, brown nose/almond eyes and full curled tail with longer furnishing. These are field observations/keeper accounts, allowing variation.

sources.title: Özbaşer et al. — Morphological and Genetic Characteristics of Zerdava (2020)
sources.evidence: Introduction and methods identify EasternBlackSea hunting/guarding population and100owned adult samples, minimum12months with older age groups. Table1 reports slightly longer-than-tall medium proportions around48–49cm, body51–52cm; typical sample fulltail29cm with white terminal7cm. Literal morphology describes erect ears, deep/wide chest, chestnut/liver coat, white ticked limbs and inward-curved longer-haired tail; Fig1page3 confirms study exemplars. No breed-purity/genetic-certainty or efficacy claim.

VBO:0201461.summary: The Cane Lupino del Gigante’s association describes strong attachment to a familiar handler. Agile and enduring, this local “Luvin” traditionally moved flocks and cattle across the steep Reggio Emilia Apennines. Preservation work began in 1997, followed by a dedicated association in 2009.
VBO:0201461.shortDescription: An agile, enduring Apennine flock dog, described by its association as strongly attached to a familiar handler.

sources.title: Cane Lupino del Gigante — Storia e tipologie
sources.evidence: Association describes special attachment to a familiar household handler, agility/endurance and traditional movement of flocks and cattle across steep Reggio Emilia Apennines. Own descriptive population account, not empirical trait guarantees.

sources.title: Cane Lupino del Gigante — Association history and current activity
sources.evidence: Own account dates preservation work to1997 and association volunteers to2009; actual May2026 gathering notice shows current living program.
